metric_rationale: The experiment is designed to pit Take The Best against Tallying by presenting option pairs where the highest-validity discriminating cue points to one option, but the overall tally of winning cues points to the other. By calculating the proportion of trials where the subject's choice aligns with the Take The Best prediction (i.e., choosing the option that wins on the first discriminating cue), we establish a metric where the TTB model will score significantly above 0.5, whereas the Tallying model will score significantly below 0.5.

This metric calculates the proportion of choices that align with the Tallying heuristic's predictions. The experimental design systematically pits Tallying against Take The Best (TTB) on every single trial. Consequently, an agent following Tallying will score close to 1.0 on this metric, whereas an agent following TTB will score close to 0.0. This stark contrast ensures maximal separation between the two theories, with minimal between-subject variance within each theory.
